questions.stem: As shown below, a magnetic dipole moment is oriented in 3 different ways in a uniform magnetic field. {{IMG_BLOCK:https://examcdn.trogon.info/qai/2026/09/26/ae6be0a1-c29e-4e03-b492-44c6141303be_12CBCH-5MagnetismMatterDPP/881ce1b7ed01.png}}

sub_parts.a: Which orientation results in the largest magnetic torque on the dipole?
sub_parts.b: Which orientation has the largest potential energy? Give a reason for your answer.

questions.answer_text: (a) $\tau$ = MB sin $\theta$ Torque is maximum when value of $\theta$ is maximum at 90° In perpendicular orientation, the angle between magnetic dipole and uniform magnetic field is 90° , hence the magnetic torque will be largest in II orientation. ($b$) $U$ = −MB cos $\theta$ For maximum potential, cos $\theta$ should be minimum, which is at 90° + $\phi$ , cos (90° + $\phi$ ) = − sin $\phi$ With sin $\phi$ , potential energy will become positive, i.$e$., $U$ = MB sin $\phi$ In I orientation, the angle between magnetic dipole and uniform magnetic field is 90° + $\phi$ , hence, the potential energy will be largest in I orientation.
questions.reasoning: (a) τ = MB sin θ Torque is maximum when value of θ is maximum at 90° In perpendicular orientation, the angle between magnetic dipole and uniform magnetic field is 90° , hence the magnetic torque will be largest in II orientation. (b) U = −MB cos θ For maximum potential, cos θ should be minimum, which is at 90° + ϕ, cos (90° + ϕ) = − sin ϕ With sin ϕ , potential energy will become positive, i.e., U = MB sin ϕ In I orientation, the angle between magnetic dipole and uniform magnetic field is 90° + ϕ , hence, the potential energy will be largest in I orientation.
questions.explanation: (a) $\tau$ = MB sin $\theta$ Torque is maximum when value of $\theta$ is maximum at 90° In perpendicular orientation, the angle between magnetic dipole and uniform magnetic field is 90° , hence the magnetic torque will be largest in II orientation. questions.stem: A bar magnet of magnetic moment 6 JT−1 aligned at 60° with uniform external magnetic field of 0.44 T. Calculate:

options.A:
the work done in turning the magnet to align its magnetic moment: 
(i) normal to the magnetic field. 
(ii) opposite to the magnetic field.
options.B: The torque on the magnet in the final orientation in case (ii).
